key_insight: A Mamba-based language model combined with data augmentation and experience replay (memory manipulation) enables sample-efficient generation of property-optimized small molecules, reusing promising candidates to cut down on costly evaluations.
problem_solved: Reduces the data and evaluation budget required to train generative models for molecular design, addressing the scarcity of labeled/expensive experimental feedback in property optimization tasks.
method: Train a Mamba-based sequence model to generate molecular representations (e.g., SMILES/SELFIES).
Use targeted data augmentation to expand training signals and diversify candidate molecules.
Implement experience replay / memory manipulation to store high-reward molecules and replay them during training for more sample-efficient optimization.
impact: Lowering the number of required evaluations and experiments speeds up iterative molecular design and makes advanced generative approaches more accessible to teams with limited compute or lab budgets.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart: model input → augmentation → generation → property evaluation → memory buffer → replay → model update.
Comparison chart: samples/evaluations required vs. baseline methods (showing reduced budget).
Memory replay schematic: buffer of high-reward molecules being reintroduced into training.
Before/after molecular examples: structures with property scores (e.g., activity or drug-likeness) to illustrate optimization.
paper_title: Sample-efficient generative molecular design using memory manipulation
paper_authors: Jeff Guo, Junwu Chen, Anthony GX-Chen, Philippe Schwaller
